p: By which is signified, that even though we are in great misery, yet there is always room for prayer.
cry come unto thee: He declares that in our prayer we must lively feel that which we desire, and steadfastly believe to obtain.
consumed like smoke: These excessive kinds of speech show how much the affliction of the Church should wound the hearts of the godly.
to eat my bread: My sorrows were so great that I did not eat.
pelican of the wilderness: Always mourning in solitude and casting out fearful cries.
sworn against me: Have conspired my death.
eaten ashes like bread: I have not risen out of my mourning to take my refreshment.
indignation and thy wrath: He shows that not only the afflictions moved him, but chiefly the feeling of God's displeasure.
endure for ever: Though we are frail, yet your promise is sure, and the remembrance of it will confirm us forever.
set time: That is, the seventy years which by the prophet Jeremiah you appointed, Jer 29:12.
stones: The more the Church is in misery and desolation, the more the faithful should love and pity it.
in his glory: That is, when he will have drawn his church out of the darkness of death.

created shall praise the LORD: The deliverance of the Church is an excellent benefit, and therefore he compares it to a new creation for in their banishment the body of the Church seemed to have been dead, which by deliverance was as it were created anew.
appointed to death: Who now in their banishment could look for nothing but death.
together: He shows that Gad's name is never more praised, than when religion flourishes and the church increases: which is chiefly accomplished under the kingdom of Christ.
weakened my strength in the way: The church lament that they see not the time of Christ, which was promised, but have but few years and short days.
They shall perish: If heaven and earth perish, much more man will perish: but the Church by reason of God's promise endures forever.
be established before thee: Seeing you have chosen your Church out of the world, and joined it to you, it cannot but continue forever: for you are everlasting.
